label: <DEL> step, content-dependent (sequences rich in e/0/n/u/f/c/w/z/o)
explanation: Low end of candidate unit 57. About 71% of activation mass is at the delimiter step, but it fires on only 8.7% of delimiter steps. Whether it fires there depends on the sequence content in a spread-out way: it is enriched when the second original token (the next output) is n/u/f/e/c/j, when the first token is o/u/c/3, and when the sequence contains e or 0. Requiring 3 or more tokens from {e,0,n,u,f,c,w,z,o} gives dev F1 0.30 and mass recall 0.59. Plain phase==1 gets mass recall 0.71 at precision 0.09. The other ~29% of mass is in the late original phase (t=4-9), mostly on first-occurrence inputs m and 1. It almost never fires in the copy phase (0.3% of mass) or at t<2. I could not separate a magnitude trend beyond the larger activations falling on the delimiter step.
